title.narrative: F.a: Social and Educational Program for the Deaf

description.narrative: Arvioiden mukaan Etiopiassa on yli 3 miljoonaa kuuroa tai kuulovammaista henkilöä, ja suurin osa heistä on kouluikäisiä lapsia ja nuoria. Kuitenkin 85 prosentilla kuulovammaisista lapsista ei ole mahdollisuutta koulutukseen. Opettajat ja koulujen hallinto Etiopiassa kannattavat yleisesti vammaisten lasten ottamista mukaan tavallisiin kouluihin, mutta opettajien koulutuksen ja opetusmateriaalien puute aiheuttaa suuria haasteita oppilaiden erityistarpeisiin vastaamiseen. Hankkeen tavoitteena on vastata näihin haasteisiin kouluttamalla opettajia ja tuottamalla korkealaatuista opetusmateriaalia. Tämän lisäksi hanke vähentää kuurona elämisen haasteita jakamalla yhteisöissä kuulovammaisuuteen liittyvää tietoa ja tukemalla kuuroja heidän pyrkimyksissään työllistyä. Hankkeen hyödynsaajia ovat vammaiset henkilöt, erityisesti kuurot, virkamiehet ja poliittise päättäjät. Hankkeen toteuttaja on Etiopian evankelisen Mekane Yesus -kirkon kehitys- ja sosiaaliasioiden komissio / South Central -synodin Kuurojenkoulu Hosainassa (EECMY-DASSC-SCS-School for the Deaf).

It is estimated that over 3 million deaf and hard of hearing (DHH) people live in Ethiopia. The majority of them are young and school-age children, and yet approximately 85% of DHH children don?t have access to education. According to the Ethiopian Ministry of Education 2019 report, the gross enrollment rate of children with disabilities is 11% which indicates that there is still a lot of work to be done to bring these children to school, and at the same time provide quality inclusive education. Teachers and schooln administrators in Ethiopia are generally in favor of mainstreaming children with disabilities into regular schools, but insufficient training of teachers and itinerant teachers along with shortages of teaching materials and resources present major challenges in addressing special educational needs of learners. The project aims to address these challenges through training of teachers on sign language, inclusive education and pedagogical skills. Moreover, high quality education materials that will improve the quality of education will be produced. The project will also address the multifaced challenge people with disabilities and deaf and hard of hearing people face through creating awareness on disability issues to the community and by providing access to gainful employment possibilities for DHH. Beneficiaries of the project are people with disabilities, especially the deaf, government officials and authorities and political desicion makers. The implementing agency is the Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus-Development and Social Services Commission-South Central Synod-School for the Deaf (EECMY-DASSC-SCS-School for the Deaf) in Hossana.
